plan.name: Cap container CPU use
plan.summary: Give every workload container Invariant launches through Docker run or create a default limit of 4 CPUs, controlled by one host environment setting, INVARIANT_CONTAINER_CPUS: unset or empty means 4, positive finite decimal counts of at least 0.01 are accepted, and invalid settings fail before container launch. Apply the same setting to the shared Docker runner and configured dependency installation and check environments, and explicitly pass it in both agents' MCP server environments so the watcher, dashboard, CLI and separate check, test and gate processes agree; preserve explicit CPU limits including the Python application runner's 1 CPU, existing memory and process limits, isolation, image acquisition, cleanup, concurrency and production deadlines. Update the named command assertions and Docker option parsers for the added CPU option, preserving their other checks; make TestSandboxNamesFailuresFromEveryShard/shard_timeout and TestSandboxQueueBudgetDoesNotRestartPerTest in sandbox_shards_accept_test.go reliable on slow machines by giving each a 15-second shared phase inside a 90-second fixture run, blocking TestBroken until canceled and scaling all 128 queue-test sleeps to 3 seconds, retaining every existing assertion and test identity; rerun those exact cases with an additional three-second startup delay in the healthy or queue-test processes, requiring both to pass while still showing phase timeout without the whole-run deadline, named interrupted work, completed healthy work, independent acceptance and a budget that never restarts per test; and extend the existing real-image sandbox budget observer to verify cpu.max and report cpu.stat usage and throttling alongside memory, process peaks and elapsed time. Report the effect on #599's two-run and three-run budget check and on representative plan checks and complete plumbing builds by comparing the uncapped base with the 4-CPU candidate on the same host and workload, identifying revisions, Docker capacity, cache state, concurrency, wall times, check versus agent time and any timeouts, with reproducible commands and measured results in docs/factory.md; unavailable Docker or network measurements remain explicit Merger work to complete before moving on, and affected real Python and TLAPS suites remain PR CI checks. Update SPEC.md with decision-cited CPU policy and update docs/factory.md and docs/gate.md with the setting, restart instructions, Python exception, per-container rather than aggregate scope and the distinction from Docker-managed image-build workers; the merger must record the new CPU policy decision under D-0105 and D-0122, preserving the existing resource and cleanup decisions.

tests.name: TestContainerCPUDefault622
tests.says: Docker run adds exactly one 4-CPU limit before the image, preserving workload arguments and non-container commands.

tests.name: TestContainerCPUOverride622
tests.says: One host setting raises or lowers the default CPU quota, while explicit container CPU limits and literal workload options retain their meaning.

tests.name: TestContainerCPUInvalid622
tests.says: Invalid CPU settings produce a named configuration error before any workload or image acquisition starts.

tests.name: TestSandboxContainerCPU622
tests.says: The real plumbing sandbox launch uses the shared default or override CPU cap while retaining its memory, PID, offline and compilation limits.

tests.name: TestConfiguredContainersCPU622
tests.says: Dependency installation, one-shot checks and persistent configured check environments all launch with the shared CPU cap and keep their existing isolation and cleanup.

tests.name: TestConfiguredContainersRejectInvalidCPU622
tests.says: Invalid CPU configuration cannot create or start any configured dependency or check container, and cleanup remains available.

tests.name: TestGateContainerCPU622
tests.says: TLC, Gobra, Nagini and TLAPS launches use the shared default and override cap, while the Python application executor keeps exactly 1 CPU and its memory and process limits.

tests.name: TestCodexMCPContainerCPU622
tests.says: The backend explicitly carries the CPU setting and existing tool allowance together in its MCP configuration, including plan, build and gate jobs.

tests.name: TestClaudeMCPContainerCPU622
tests.says: The other backend supplies the same CPU setting in its MCP environment without losing the tool allowance or adding a server to review jobs.

tests.name: TestSandboxShardTimeoutWithSlowHealthyTest622
tests.says: The existing shard_timeout case still passes every assertion when its healthy fixture test takes three extra seconds to start: phase timeout fails the sandbox without the whole-run deadline, names the interrupted test, and preserves healthy and independent acceptance results.

tests.name: TestSandboxSharedBudgetWithSlowQuickTests622
tests.says: The existing shared-queue-budget fixture still passes every assertion when each queued fixture test takes three extra seconds to start: some tests complete, some remain unstarted, the phase times out without renewing per test or consuming the whole-run deadline, and independent acceptance reports.

usage.summary: Wrote the revised plan and acceptance tests, preserving the original scope and adding both slow-machine fixture checks. Validation remains incomplete: the check tool timed out twice after 900 seconds.
